documents.text: Families who lived there and about their efforts to provide for the needs of the travelers. Ira Hinckley, his brother Arza, and local workmen built the fort of volcanic rock in 1855. They built it to protect themselves and travelers from possible Native American raids resulting from the Black Hawk War (1865–68). Native Americans never attacked the fort. During the fort’s use as a way station, the Hinckley family maintained good relationships with local Pahvant Ute and Navajo Indians. Operating a self-sufficient fort was largely a family affair.
